messages.author: 2d0c82c04a2db6dc
messages.subject: Defoliation
parts:
Hello dears
I'm new to all things geometric morphometrics, however I have a question. I am carrying out a defoliation exercise on plants, there is an insect that feeds on the leaves, I would like to know. Is there any method within geometric morphometry that allows me to estimate the shape of the leaf margin after having been defoliated? this with the objective of determining how much biomass the plant lost because of this insect.
If anyone knows information about this I would be very grateful if you tell me what method I could use.
Jimmy Reyes
University of Pamplona

messages.author: 8bafa9b5ef506689
messages.subject: Re: Defoliation
parts:
Hi Jimmy,

For estimating loss of biomass I might simply look at area loss; I.e. measure before and after (or group means) of area by making outlines in something like imagej. 

If you are interested in shape differences, I think your problem is tricky because you won’t have landmarks (homologous points between specimens). One approach you might look into is Fourier shape analysis, which for 2D seems fairly straightforward. 

Katie
